confidence.rationale: This is the current official RDoC construct definition, used for alignment rather than as a complete theory of all memory systems.

limitations: RDoC is an evolving research framework and does not make every memory task or neural signal equivalent to the construct.

scope.population: Research framework spanning normal-to-abnormal human functioning.
scope.temporal_scope: Current NIMH RDoC framework as accessed on 2026-08-26.

claims.statement: RDoC Declarative Memory covers encoding, storage, consolidation, and retrieval of representations of facts and events.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Each encoding condition follows the reported orienting-question procedure.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Controlled condition assignment and counterbalancing reduce stable participant and item confounding, subject to source-specific implementation details.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Participants or counterbalanced items were represented across the compared encoding conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Within-protocol difference in later recognition performance after meaning-based versus structural or phonemic encoding questions.

confidence.rationale: Ten controlled experiments supported a robust within-protocol encoding effect, while historical reporting and task specificity limit quantitative generalization.

limitations: The effect establishes an encoding-condition difference but does not uniquely identify one memory mechanism or guarantee transfer to other materials and retrieval tests.

boundary_conditions: Words, incidental orienting questions, later recognition, and the specific structural, phonemic, and semantic comparisons reported in the source.
scope.population: Undergraduate participants in ten experiments reported by Craik and Tulving in 1975.
scope.temporal_scope: Encoding questions followed by an unexpected recognition test within the reported sessions.

claims.statement: In the reported incidental-learning experiments, meaning-based encoding questions increased later word recognition relative to structural or phonemic questions.
claims.temporal_ordering: The assigned orienting question preceded word encoding and the later recognition response.

confidence.rationale: The cases show a striking within-person dissociation, but the sample is three, lesion extent is not experimentally assigned, and population generalization is limited.

claims.confounding_note: Developmental plasticity, lesion extent beyond the hippocampus, premorbid differences, education, and measurement choice can influence the observed profile.

estimate.notes: Pronounced episodic amnesia coexisted with speech, literacy, and factual knowledge in the low-average to average range.

limitations: The result supports separability of measured memory functions but does not prove that the hippocampus is unnecessary for all semantic learning.

boundary_conditions: Clinical case series with early pathology and extensive neuropsychological characterization.
scope.population: Three individuals with early-onset bilateral hippocampal pathology described by Vargha-Khadem and colleagues in 1997.
scope.temporal_scope: Childhood injury followed by assessment in adolescence or early adulthood.

claims.statement: In three reported developmental-amnesia cases with early hippocampal pathology, severe episodic-memory impairment coexisted with substantially better semantic knowledge and academic attainment.

confidence.rationale: Controlled encoding effects are consistent with elaboration and distinctiveness, but the experiments did not isolate one unique latent process.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened if preregistered manipulations equating elaboration and distinctiveness eliminate their contribution while a semantic-versus-shallow recognition advantage remains reliably attributable to another process.
limitations: Semantic processing, semantic memory, elaboration, distinctiveness, and retrieval match must not be collapsed into one construct.

boundary_conditions: The task must induce meaningful analysis and later test memory for the studied items.
scope.population: Humans performing incidental word-encoding tasks followed by recognition.
scope.temporal_scope: Meaning analysis during encoding through later recognition.

claims.statement: Meaning-based encoding may improve later episodic recognition by producing a more elaborated and distinctive representation of the studied item.
claims.temporal_ordering: Meaning-based analysis occurs during study before formation and later retrieval of the tested representation.

evidence.design: Ten experiments manipulating word-encoding questions and measuring later recognition or retention.

effect.metric: recognition after semantic versus phonemic or structural encoding
effect.notes: Meaning-based questions generally produced higher later retention; processing time alone did not account for the pattern in follow-up experiments.

evidence.extraction_locator: Article summary and experiments I-X comparing structural, phonemic, and semantic orienting questions followed by unexpected retention tests.
limitations: Historical multi-experiment report without a pooled modern effect estimate or preregistration.
evidence.population: Undergraduate participants in the reported experiments; total sample size was not extracted as one pooled number.
evidence.summary: Controlled meaning-based encoding conditions produced better later word memory than shallower structural or sound-based conditions.

evidence.design: Neuropsychological and neuroanatomical case series of three people with early-onset amnesia.

effect.notes: Severe everyday episodic amnesia occurred alongside low-average to average speech, literacy, and factual knowledge.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract describing three cases, early injury, episodic amnesia, schooling, language, literacy, and factual knowledge.
limitations: Very small selected case series; pathology and developmental adaptation were not experimentally controlled.
evidence.population: Three individuals with injury at birth, by age four, or at age nine.
evidence.summary: Three developmental-amnesia cases showed much greater impairment of episodic remembering than of acquired semantic knowledge.

evidence.design: Follow-up encoding experiments testing alternatives to a simple processing-time explanation of later retention.

effect.metric: retention pattern after qualitative encoding manipulations
effect.notes: Results were consistent with qualitative semantic elaboration and congruity rather than processing duration alone.

evidence.extraction_locator: Article summary and experiments V-X addressing processing duration, decision type, congruity, and qualitative encoding differences.
limitations: The proposed internal representation was inferred from task contrasts rather than directly measured or uniquely manipulated.
evidence.population: Undergraduate participants in the reported experiments.
evidence.summary: Follow-up experiments supported qualitative meaning-based encoding over a simple longer-processing-time explanation.

metadata.description: Separates memory constructs, encoding manipulation, recognition behavior, performance measurement, neuropsychological dissociation, and an elaborative-encoding mechanism hypothesis.
metadata.title: Primary evidence pack for declarative, episodic, and semantic memory

boundary_notes: Declarative memory is broader than episodic memory and semantic memory considered separately.
The construct is not identical to a recognition score or to one neural structure.
objects.definition: Acquisition, storage, consolidation, and retrieval of representations of facts and events that can support flexible use of relational information.

external_mappings.rationale: The PMM label and definition follow the current official RDoC construct page while preserving narrower child constructs separately.

objects.label: Declarative memory

boundary_notes: Episodic memory is not equivalent to all long-term memory or to recognition performance alone.
objects.definition: Memory for events together with spatial, temporal, or other contextual relations that locate what happened within a particular episode.

external_mappings.rationale: The external concept is marked Unreviewed; PMM therefore preserves the alignment without importing its asserted hierarchy as settled.

objects.label: Episodic memory

boundary_notes: Semantic memory as stored knowledge is not the same object as semantic processing performed during an encoding task.
objects.definition: Organized knowledge of concepts, word meanings, and facts that is not tied to remembering one specific learning episode.

external_mappings.rationale: The labels are close, but the Cognitive Atlas record is marked Unreviewed and contains task assertions that PMM does not treat as validated automatically.

objects.label: Semantic memory

boundary_notes: This task samples particular encoding and recognition operations; it is not declarative memory itself.
objects.definition: Laboratory task in which participants answer questions about words without initially expecting a later old-new memory test.

dimensions.encoding: structural, phonemic, or semantic orienting questions

external_mappings.rationale: The PMM task is one narrower incidental-encoding implementation of the broader unreviewed recognition-memory task record.

objects.label: Incidental word-encoding and recognition task
objects.scope: Human laboratory studies using incidental encoding questions followed by a recognition test.

boundary_notes: A small lesion case series can demonstrate a dissociation pattern but cannot estimate a population-average causal effect.
objects.definition: Clinical assessment context comparing episodic remembering and acquired factual knowledge after early bilateral hippocampal pathology.

dimensions.onset: birth to nine years in the indexed case series
dimensions.pathology: bilateral hippocampal damage or marked volume reduction

objects.label: Developmental-amnesia neuropsychological assessment
objects.scope: The three developmental-amnesia cases described by Vargha-Khadem and colleagues in 1997.

objects.definition: Experimental assignment of structural, phonemic, or meaning-based questions about each study word before a later memory test.
objects.delivery: Present protocol-defined orienting questions about word appearance, sound, category, or sentence meaning during incidental encoding.
objects.label: Encoding-question depth manipulation

objects.definition: Observable response indicating whether a test item was encountered during the earlier study phase.
objects.label: Old-new recognition response
objects.response_topography: Protocol-defined old or new judgment for each test word.

objects.definition: Correct discrimination of previously studied words from unstudied words on the later recognition test.
objects.label: Later word-recognition accuracy

boundary_notes: Recognition accuracy reflects both memory discrimination and response policy unless the design and analysis separate them.
objects.definition: Condition-specific hits, misses, false alarms, correct rejections, or a derived discrimination measure from an old-new test.
objects.label: Old-new recognition-memory measurement
objects.method: Administer an old-new recognition test after encoding and compare prespecified response measures between encoding conditions.

boundary_notes: Relative preservation does not mean completely normal semantic memory, and test batteries do not make the constructs process-identical.
objects.definition: A battery comparing memory for personally experienced events with language, literacy, and factual-knowledge attainment.
objects.label: Episodic-semantic neuropsychological profile
objects.method: Integrate standardized neuropsychological tests and real-life memory characterization across episodic and semantic domains.

boundary_notes: Superior memory after semantic questions does not uniquely identify elaboration, distinctiveness, congruity, or one neural implementation.
objects.definition: Proposed process in which a new item is analyzed for meaning and related to contextual or existing knowledge, producing a more discriminable later memory representation.
objects.label: Elaborative semantic encoding
realization_conditions: The encoding question requires meaningful analysis rather than only visual or phonological classification.
Later retrieval can use information made distinctive or relational during encoding.
